name: Stars of the Lid
label: Kranky
lede: Adam Wiltzie and Brian McBride started a band in Austin on Christmas Day 1992 and spent thirty years trading tapes and making music slow enough that it barely admits to moving. Along the way they named a song after Fulham's football ground.

eras.title: Christmas Day in Austin
eras.text: Adam Wiltzie and Brian McBride started Stars of the Lid in Austin, where McBride had moved in 1990. The early records were rough and tape-hissy, closer to drone rock than the orchestral stillness that came later.

years.big: "Your own personal cinema, located between your eye and eyelid."
years.src: Wikipedia · Wikipedia: Adam Wiltzie · Wikipedia: Brian McBride
years.h: Adam Wiltzie and Brian McBride start a band on Christmas Day
years.p: Brian McBride, a debate kid from Irving, Texas, and Adam Wiltzie, a New Yorker whose youth tennis career ended with a knee injury at 16, start Stars of the Lid in Austin on December 25, 1992. McBride's gloss on the name is above.
years.xp: The name is the lights you see with your eyes shut: phosphenes, the shapes that float behind your eyelids. The pair loved Arvo Pärt, Gavin Bryars, Górecki, Brian Eno and [[Talk Talk|a74f43e4-50c4-4b19-a2ce-c05ce9bccb03]].

years.h: Sedimental, a small label, puts out Music for Nitrous Oxide
years.p: Brian McBride and Adam Wiltzie recorded it in 1993 and 1994 with a third member, Kirk Laktas. After it, Stars of the Lid is a duo for good.

yt: Full set at Other Music, New York, June 27, 1996
years.h: Austin's Trance Syndicate pairs them with Labradford
years.p: The split 12-inch is The Kahanek Incident, Vol. 3, shared with Richmond's [[Labradford|7cf7ef41-9637-4bf2-ae99-d8d6611ccdc6]]. The same year brings album two, Gravitational Pull vs. the Desire for an Aquatic Life.

eras.title: Twin Peaks and the DAT tapes
eras.text: Kranky signed them in 1997 and the records got longer, quieter and stranger. By 2001 Wiltzie was moving to Brussels and McBride was in Chicago, so they made a double album by mail.

years.h: The Ballasted Orchestra starts the Kranky years
years.p: Made in East Austin. Two tracks are titled "Music for Twin Peaks Episode #30", "Taphead" is named after the [[Talk Talk|a74f43e4-50c4-4b19-a2ce-c05ce9bccb03]] track, and "The Artificial Pine Arch Song" runs 20:52 on vinyl.

years.h: Per Aspera Ad Astra, plus a split single with Windsor for the Derby
years.p: The limited EP Maneuvering the Nocturnal Hum comes out the same year, and the split single is with [[Windsor for the Derby|04fc2164-c46d-4d0d-851d-13467b444b84]].

years.h: After Avec Laudenum, no more single-disc albums
years.p: Kranky releases the last one-disc Stars of the Lid studio album. The next two are both doubles.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Tired Sounds of Stars of the Lid
years.h: A double album gets built out of mailed DAT tapes
years.p: Adam Wiltzie was moving from Austin to Brussels and Brian McBride was in Chicago, so they sent DAT tapes back and forth. The Tired Sounds of Stars of the Lid runs 123 minutes and sold about 5,000 at first, 10,000 within three years.
years.xp:
Wiltzie worked on an Akai MPC 2000 and McBride on an Ensoniq ASR-10 sampler, each at home. "Gasfarming" samples dialogue from Twin Peaks.

Pitchfork later ranked it the sixth best ambient album of all time.

eras.title: The hundredth record
eras.text: Both men made side records, then put everything into a second double album. It was Kranky's hundredth release, and it's the one most people mean when they say Stars of the Lid.

years.h: Wiltzie and Christina Vantzou start The Dead Texan
years.p: Adam Wiltzie teams with visual artist Christina Vantzou on [[The Dead Texan|18c2f08b-bdac-4877-9865-e5461317c1a6]], released on Kranky.

years.h: McBride goes solo with When the Detail Lost Its Freedom
years.p: It's Brian McBride's first record under his own name.

years.src: Wikipedia: And Their Refinement of the Decline
years.h: And Their Refinement of the Decline becomes Kranky's 100th release
years.p: Two hours long, made in Brussels and Los Angeles with cellists, brass, harp and the Saint-Jean-Baptiste au Béguinage children's choir. Metacritic scores it 87.
years.xp:
"Don't Bother They're Here" uses the melody of Stephen Sondheim's "Send in the Clowns."

"Dopamine Clouds Over Craven Cottage" is named for Fulham's ground, and by coincidence shares a name with Fulham's captain at the time.

years.cap: Stars of the Lid on stage at All Tomorrow's Parties
years.h: Strings join the world tour, and a CD goes on sale at the merch table
years.p: In Europe a string trio of Lucinda Chua, Noura Sanatian and Ela Baruch plays with the duo; in North America it's Julia Kent on cello. The 59-minute Carte-de-Visite is sold only on tour.
years.xp: The tour ran through 2007 and 2008. Somewhere Cold voted the band Artist of the Year in December 2007.

eras.title: One-offs and other bands
eras.text: Stars of the Lid never broke up, but after the tour it mostly lived in occasional shows. Wiltzie found a second audience with A Winged Victory for the Sullen, and McBride made music about disappearing bees.

years.cap: Brian McBride with the Wordless Music Orchestra, Brooklyn
years.h: Brian McBride scores a documentary about vanishing bees
years.p: McBride's The Effective Disconnect is the soundtrack to Vanishing of the Bees. He also starts Bell Gardens with Kenneth James Gibson.

years.h: Adam Wiltzie and Dustin O'Halloran form A Winged Victory for the Sullen
years.p: The duo's first record as [[A Winged Victory for the Sullen|67c179d3-f358-43bf-8ecc-d9c560878b65]] comes out on Erased Tapes. It becomes Wiltzie's second audience.

eras.title: The unfinished album
eras.text: Brian McBride died in 2023 with an album's worth of Stars of the Lid sessions from the 2010s still unreleased. Adam Wiltzie has said he intends to finish it.

years.h: Brian McBride dies at 53 in Los Angeles
years.p: He died of natural causes. Away from music he coached policy debate at USC and directed a University of Texas debate camp.

years.big: "Someday I am going to try to do this for everyone."
years.h: Wiltzie says the sessions Brian McBride left behind will come out
years.p: Adam Wiltzie tells The Guardian from Brussels that there's an album's worth of recordings from the 2010s.
years.xp: Wiltzie's words come from a Guardian interview on August 30, 2023, five days after McBride's death. The band never officially ended.
